html:
The Yurutí, or Wajiara, are a small people of the Vaupés region on the border of Colombia and Brazil. Their language is one of the Tucanoan languages, with about 1,200 speakers.

Like their neighbours the Cubeo, Tatuyo and Wanano, they belong to a regional system in which people must marry someone from a group that speaks a different language. As a result most people in the Vaupés speak several languages. They live in longhouses by the rivers, growing bitter manioc and fishing.
